llm.summary: This skill is a focused Apple jobs lookup helper that uses a disclosed Crawlora API key and external API calls, with no evidence of hidden persistence, privilege escalation, or unrelated data access.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires network access to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 and sends the Crawlora API key plus user-supplied job query parameters, which is disclosed and proportionate to the API-backed research purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time script, package installation, dependency fetching, or agent behavior modification was found; setup is limited to obtaining and setting CRAWLORA_API_KEY.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs use of a bundled shell helper and examples pipe to jq, but the helper is route-limited, GET-only, fixes the API base URL, and rejects unsupported methods and paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism or elevated execution was found; the helper creates a temporary curl config for the API key with restrictive permissions and removes it on exit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to search public Apple job postings and fetch posting details; the artifacts implement that through documented GET-only Crawlora endpoints for Apple Jobs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using Crawlora as a third-party API provider for Apple jobs searches. Keep CRAWLORA_API_KEY in the environment, avoid placing sensitive personal data in search queries, and be aware that successful API calls may consume Crawlora credits.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The shell helper is expected for this skill's API workflow. The lack of an explicit allowed-tools declaration is a packaging/least-privilege note, but the artifact itself constrains requests to documented Apple Jobs GET routes.
[E1] expected: External transmission to Crawlora is disclosed in SKILL.md and is necessary for the skill's stated function; reviewed artifacts show the transmitted data is the API key header and user-provided job search/detail parameters.
[PE2] unexpected: The cited chmod 600 is not sudo or root execution; it restricts a temporary curl config file containing the API key and is removed via trap on exit.
